candidates.old:
LDY #0
    LDA act                         \ the player (slot 0) goes on last: when listed, it is first
    BNE put_on_test
    INY
.put_on_test
    CPY act_n                       \ (unsigned: act_n may be 0 with a stale player entry)
    BCS put_on_player
.putting_on
    LDX act,Y
    BIT need,X                      \ V = bit 6, it goes on: put_on's own test, done here
    BVC next_put_on
    PHY                             \ 65C02 opcode
    JSR put_on.going_on
    PLY                             \ 65C02 opcode
.next_put_on
    INY
    CPY act_n
    BCC putting_on
.put_on_player
    LDX #0
    JSR put_on
    LDA #&04
    STA os_ram_copy_of_currently_selected_rom
    STA romsel
.player_done
    LDA back                        \ for the vsync interrupt to show, at the pass lock's field
    STA flip_screen
    LDA crtc_start_address_high
    STA flip_crtc_hi
    LDA crtc_start_address_low
    STA flip_crtc_lo
    JSR cpu_sees_main
candidates.new:
LDY #1                          \ the player (slot 0) goes on last: when listed, it is first
    LDA act
    BEQ put_on_test
    DEY
.put_on_test
    CPY act_n                       \ (unsigned: act_n may be 0 with a stale player entry)
    BCS put_on_player
.putting_on
    LDX act,Y
    BIT need,X                      \ V = bit 6, it goes on: put_on's own test, done here
    BVC next_put_on
    STY ren_k                       \ ren_k is dead here (take_off's and the scroll's)
    JSR put_on.going_on
    LDY ren_k
.next_put_on
    INY
    CPY act_n
    BCC putting_on
.put_on_player
    BIT need                        \ the player (slot 0): V = bit 6, it goes on (put_on's own test, done here)
    BVC pon_player_off
    LDX #0
    JSR put_on.going_on
.pon_player_off
    LDA #&04
    STA os_ram_copy_of_currently_selected_rom
    STA romsel
.player_done
    LDX back                        \ for the vsync interrupt to show, at the pass lock's field
    STX flip_screen
    LDX crtc_start_address_high
    STX flip_crtc_hi
    LDX crtc_start_address_low
    STX flip_crtc_lo
    TRB acccon                      \ A = &04: X = 0, the CPU sees main again (cpu_sees_main as one read-modify-write; I = 0, as cpu_sees_back's CLI left it)
candidates.summary: Candidate 1 plus STY ren_k / LDY ren_k in place of PHY/PLY around the put-on of a listed mover (6 cycles for 7, 2 bytes more; alternative to 1, 2, 3). MEASURED in a scratch copy (bench build = unshifted DEBUG_LIVES, pcprof seed 1, 1500 passes, work a pass without the wait): control 35625.28; this one 35602.25, a saving of 23.03 a pass (assembles; passlock seed 3, 800 passes, state and screen identical).
candidates.equivalence: The player is slot 0: the old LDX #0; JSR put_on runs put_on's BIT need,X (X = 0, so BIT need) and either RTS (V clear) or BVS going_on with X = 0. New: BIT need (zero page, 3 cycles) does the test here; V clear skips to the ROMSEL restore; V set loads X = 0 and JSR put_on.going_on, the entry the loop already uses, with V = 1 as on every arrival there. C at going_on: the old player path arrived with C = 1 and the new arrives with C = 1 as well (BIT leaves C; the loop exit has C = 1 either way), the loop's own arrival has C = 0, so going_on does not depend on C. In the not-going case X is no longer 0 afterwards: nothing reads X after (LDA #&04, the ROMSEL stores, the flip stores, restore_game_zp, callers ignore X). need is zero page (&1F, ren_zp's first byte), so BIT need is the zp form (opcode &24, 3 cycles, 2 bytes). Measured (seed 1, 1500 passes, build/grind/pc-seed1.json): put_on's BIT ran 1499 times, BVS taken 1018 (goes on), RTS 481 (does not): 68% go on, so the saving is 2 cycles when it does (BIT 3 + BVC 2 + LDX 2 + JSR 6 = 13 vs LDX 2 + JSR 6 + BIT zp,X 4 + BVS taken 3 = 15) and 14 when it does not (BIT 3 + BVC taken 3 = 6 vs 2 + 6 + 4 + 2 + RTS 6 = 20): 0.68*2 + 0.32*14 = 5.8 a pass. Holding RIGHT: always goes on, 2. cpu_sees_main is SEI; LDA acccon; AND #&FB; STA acccon; CLI; RTS: it clears ACCCON bit 2 (X) and nothing else. TRB acccon with A = &04 clears exactly bit 2 in one read-modify-write (65C02 TRB abs: two reads, one write; no interrupt can fall inside one instruction, so the SEI that guarded the read-then-write against the vsync handler's own ACCCON read-modify-write is not needed; jsbeeb's TRB: read, modify, write). The CLI is not needed because I is already 0: render is entered by render_pass and render_to_main (after wait_for_flip, which needs interrupts running), cpu_sees_back at line 346 ends in CLI on both its paths, and nothing between there and here executes SEI unpaired (grep SEI/CLI/PLP/PHP over src: render.6502 and kindcache_build.6502 have only SEI..CLI pairs; the other hits are in code render never calls). A = &04 at .player_done: the only way in is the fall-through from LDA #&04 / STA romsel (grep: nothing branches or jumps to player_done; tools/passcost.mjs uses it only as a profile label). Loading the three flip values through X: LDX zp is 3 cycles/2 bytes like LDA zp, STX abs 4/3 like STA abs; flip_screen, flip_crtc_hi, flip_crtc_lo get the same bytes in the same order. On leaving: old A = acccon AND &FB, new A = &04, X = crtc low (old X whatever put_on left), flags differ (TRB sets Z): restore_game_zp starts with LDA and reads no X/Y/flag; render_pass's caller (wait_for_timer_281a) does SEI; LDA field_count; render_finish's callers load LDY #/LDX # or JMP; render_to_main does SEI; LDX #&0C. Nothing reads A, X, Y or any flag on return. (The analysis shows V live out of the window; every consumer above ignores it, and the old V was whatever the last ADC in a draw left.) cpu_sees_main stays: cpu_sees_back branches to it. LDY #1; LDA act; BEQ put_on_test; DEY gives Y = 1 when act[0] = 0 (the player listed, so the loop starts after it) and Y = 0 otherwise, exactly as LDY #0; LDA act; BNE put_on_test; INY did, with A = act at put_on_test in both. Measured: act[0] = 0 every pass (the BNE is never taken in the profile), so the common path is LDY 2 + LDA 4 + BEQ taken 3 = 9 cycles against 2 + 4 + 2 + INY 2 = 10. ren_k (zero page &4E) is written/read in render.6502 only in the take-off loop, the scroll's apply_entries and mark_to_draw/close_over_overlaps (lines 483-509, 1011-1087), all finished before section 6; the put-on code (put_on, draw_mover, sky_put_on, compact, kc_*) never names it (grep src). STY zp 3 + LDY zp 3 = 6 vs PHY 3 + PLY 4 = 7, 1.3 draws a pass.
candidates.relies_on: Grows the code by 6 bytes, so everything after .put_on_player in bank 4 slides up 6. In the bench build (unshifted DEBUG_LIVES) that is cpu_sees_back/main (&9379), wait_for_flip, render_to_main, ren_plot_lives, lives_digits (&9444) and write_column (&9644) and on. Page crossings moved: ren_plot_lives' fast_row loop (&93EF-&93F6) goes to &93F5-&93FC, still in page &93 (BPL fast_row stays in-page); its by_cell code crosses &9400 already; lives_digits,Y (digit 5's block already crosses a page) moves 6 bytes and runs only on a lives change; write_column's and the later renderer code's branches and indexed reads may change page status and only the gate's measurement settles that. The window's own loop (putting_on &9347-&9356) does not move: the growth is after it. Also relies on I = 0 here, TRB abs atomic against the vsync handler, A = &04 from the LDA #&04 above, nothing branching to player_done, need being zero page, and put_on.going_on being a callable entry (the loop already calls it). The two shifted candidates (1, 4) lose cycles to a slide: in the control the branch ending at &97FC (close_over_overlaps' loop, cycles at &97FA 12.9 a pass) has its next-pc in page &97 with its target; shifted by 4 to 7 bytes its next-pc is in page &98 and its target in &97, so it pays the taken-branch page-cross cycle (17.2 a pass, +4.3), and &9DD0 loses 1.5 more; a shift of 0-3 or 8 or more would not. Without the slide, 1 would save 26.8 and 4 would save 28.1.
